newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine church attacks country's legal system.
newsitem.headline: Argentine church attacks country's legal system.

text.p: Argentina's Catholic Church said on Saturday that corruption and a lack of independence in the legal system threatened to "create a crisis of the country's social cohesion."

"The legal system requires a clear independence from the powers of the state and from the professional corporations and unions," the country's bishops said in a statement issued on the final day of a Church conference on Argentina's legal system, state news agency Telam reported.

The bishops said there was a value crisis that included a "sensation of wanting to live without laws, of wanting to modify them to serve sectorial interests," which "facilitates public and private corruption."
"This creates a generalized state of incredulity, of fear of others, of impotence and anguish which impedes the formation of a spirit of solidarity," they said.

Argentina's Catholic Church has a track record of being an active critic of political authorities and the government. It has taken a tough stance against President Carlos Menem's neo-liberal economic policies that have pushed unemployment above 17 percent of the work force.
The statement issued by the bishops refers "implicitly to recent scandals brought about by various magistrates."
